body.statement: For \(K=2\), a size-three cluster, and \(r_{3,1}=1\), the three label-one control-exposure coordinates are pairwise jointly observable but are not jointly observable as a triple. Hence no pairwise conflict graph has independent sets equal to the feasible observation sets of this exact-count experiment, whereas \(H\) retains the correct triple obstruction.
body.justification: The proposition identifies the first combinatorial obstruction that a graph surrogate deletes.
body.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition 2.2, characterizes its arbitrary-neighborhood-interference experiment through a pairwise conflict graph; the exact-count saturation channel has higher-order feasibility constraints.
body.consumer: Certificate builders can reject graph-based kernels before they generate invalid risks or designs for fixed-count saturation trials.
